text:
alice_dev: Heads up — saw a production routing anomaly where requests from partner-proxy are being routed to the wrong tenant when X-Customer-ID is missing.

samir_engineer: Can you paste the original header chain? Is the proxy adding any X-Forwarded-* or X-Route-Hint?

alice_dev: here's a typical header set we saw:

  X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
  X-Forwarded-Proto: https
  User-Agent: partner-proxy/2.3
  X-Customer-ID: 
  X-Route-Hint: partner123

lee_platform: so X-Customer-ID empty but X-Route-Hint present — our gateway currently treats X-Customer-ID as highest precedence then X-Route-Hint then inferred UA. That means empty X-Customer-ID falls through to route-hint (which is fine) — what's the issue?

alice_dev: the problem is some proxies strip X-Route-Hint but forward a stale User-Agent that matches another tenant's partner SDK; UA inference routed to wrong tenant. We need more robust precedence + spoof protection.

priya_sre: +1. We should not trust UA for tenant selection unless it's paired with signed assertion. Two options: (1) enforce signed X-Route-Signature header (HMAC over route+ts) from trusted proxies; (2) normalize precedence: auth token -> signed route header -> customer-id -> route-hint -> UA fallback.

samir_engineer: for option (1) what's the key distribution model? customers have different proxies/keys; we'd need a key registry and rotation API on the control plane.

lee_platform: we already have a per-customer KMS entry for Private deployments, but hosted customers would need either a key-per-proxy or a shared signing token. Also we should strip user-controlled X-Customer-ID at the edge unless it's signed.

alice_dev: I can prototype an nginx sidecar config to validate signature. Example check:

  proxy_set_header X-Route-Signature $http_x_route_signature;
  access_by_lua_block {
    -- validate HMAC against registry (customer_id + timestamp)
  }

priya_sre: Also add telemetry: emit routing_decision with reason enum (signed_header, auth_token, customer_id, route_hint, ua_inferred) and include fields: matched_header, header_present, signature_valid. That will make debugging much easier.

samir_engineer: UX note — console should show the per-request routing_reason and the raw header chain in trace view. For rollouts, canary the signed-header enforcement behind a feature flag per-region.

lee_platform: agree. I'll open a PR for header precedence change + telemetry + feature-flag rollout. tagging infra-bot to run the canary test.

infra-bot: Canary job queued: routing-signed-header-enforce — 50 hosts in us-west — waiting for results.

alice_dev: thanks — will follow up with test cases for proxy chain simulations and a quick doc on migration steps (strip/normalize at edge, key provisioning). :thumbsup:
